verdict.rationale: Phaser has a long history, official docs, and community members explicitly praise its abundance of examples and docs (phaser-docs example pages, phaser-comm-7, phaser-comm-10, phaser-comm-18), which supports LLM familiarity. However, there are concrete, documented caveats: the API has undergone major version churn (Phaser 2→3→4, with docs explicitly warning that Phaser-2-era code 'likely won't work' in Phaser 3, phaser-docs-7), TypeScript support is described as only 'best-effort' via DefinitelyTyped rather than native (phaser-comm-8), and independent hands-on comments call the documentation itself 'the worst I've seen' and note gaps that TypeScript+VSCode had to compensate for (phaser-comm-16, phaser-comm-4). These are concrete counter-signals that LLM-generated code targeting an older/newer API version may not work first try. Missing for 10: first-party evidence of LLM-specific benchmarking or explicit AI-training-data curation, and resolution of the version-drift/documentation-quality complaints.
